title: When life starts asking what it is for
issueStatement: The day may be full, but the soul keeps asking what all this movement is finally serving, and ordinary responsibilities begin to feel spiritually thin.
centralInsight: Gurbani frames human life as opportunity for meeting, service, and Naam. Purpose becomes clearer when life is received as entrusted, not merely consumed as maintenance.
practicalReflection: Purpose usually thins out in the middle of ordinary duty, not only in crisis. The correction matters because it asks whether this very day is being answered like a calling or merely managed.
actionPrompt: Before the next task swallows the hour, choose one act that answers life as calling instead of maintenance.
searchTerms: building a life that keeps its purpose

excerpts.explanation: The line turns calling toward praise and holy usefulness, not self-importance or spiritual careerism.

practice.label: Steady Practice
practice.title: When purpose needs a repeatable shape
practice.issueStatement: The day fills up, but the inner reason for being here keeps thinning out. Purpose rarely disappears in one decision; it is usually spent away in a hundred necessary-looking motions.
practice.centralInsight: Guru names human life as rare opportunity for meeting, service, and Naam. A real practice of purpose therefore has to rescue the day from maintenance, not from drama.
practice.practicalReflection: A believable rule for purpose survives the dull hour. If it only works when you feel stirred, drift will outlast it.
practice.actionPrompt: Choose one hinge in the day, the first task, the lunch break, or the doorway home. At that cue, name one act of service before the day spends itself on maintenance.
